issues.display_title: Issue #43: Implement Stripe Billing Access API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/07/26

✅ Implementation:

Example Billing Status API

Endpoint: GET /v1/billing/status
Description: Returns the current subscription status, plan name, and renewal/expiration date for the authenticated user.

Example cURL Request

curl -X GET http://localhost:9999/v1/billing/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_session_token>"

Success Response (Active Subscription)

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 14,
  "data": {
    "status": "active",
    "plan": "price_1...",
    "started_at": "2026-07-02T10:00:00Z",
    "expires_at": "2026-08-02T10:00:00Z"
  }
}

Success Response (No Active Subscription)

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 12,
  "data": {
    "status": "inactive"
  }
}

Error Responses

Unauthorized (No session token):

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "requestTime": 5,
  "data": {
    "error": "unauthorized"
  }
}

Example Billing Portal API

Endpoint: POST /v1/billing/portal
Description: Opens the Stripe hosted billing portal to allow authenticated users to manage their existing subscriptions, update payment methods, or cancel their plan.

Example cURL Request

curl -X POST http://localhost:9999/v1/billing/portal \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_session_token>"

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 98,
  "data": {
    "url": "https://billing.stripe.com/p/session/test_..."
  }
}

Error Responses

Bad Request (No existing Stripe Customer record):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "requestTime": 20,
  "data": {
    "error": "no billing history"
  }
}

Unauthorized (No session token):

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "requestTime": 12,
  "data": {
    "error": "unauthorized"
  }
}

Implementation: Stripe Billing Access API

Overview

This task ensures that the API securely gates access to billing-related endpoints, distinguishing between public actions and authenticated actions that require a valid user session.

Code Implementation

The implementation relies on Fiber's routing groups to strictly segregate the endpoints:

  1. Routing Setup (src/routes/v1/billing.go):

    • Authenticated routes are grouped using billing.Group("/", middleware.Auth()), enforcing JWT authentication before accessing sensitive actions.
    • Public routes (like /webhook and /catalog) are kept separate.

  2. Access Control Logic (src/action/v1/billing/status.go & portal.go):

    • Both Status and Portal handlers immediately verify the session identity via middleware.GetUser(c). If unauthenticated, a 401 Unauthorized is returned.
    • For Status, the endpoint securely checks the database for the active subscription using GORM: config.DB.Where("user_id = ?", user.UniqueID).
    • The logic strictly differentiates between a generic system error and a legitimate absence of a subscription (errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound)). If the record is absent, it returns an "inactive" state rather than an error, safely restricting the user without breaking the frontend experience.

Security

  • Credentials and endpoints are injected via environment variables (e.g., FRONTEND_URL and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY), avoiding hardcoded values.
  • A shared getFrontendURL() helper securely falls back to safe defaults if environment variables are missing.

﻿## Document Paths

  • Brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_access_api_brainstorming.md
  • Implementation plan: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_access_api_plan.md
  • Branch: product-docs
  • Master billing brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md

Purpose

Create an API that answers what an account or project can use right now based on billing state.

The app should not guess access from frontend state. It should ask the API for the current billing access view.

Expected Experience

When the website or app asks for billing access, the API should return a clear answer for the current account and, when relevant, a specific project.

The answer should explain access from:

  • Base account subscription
  • Published project hosting
  • Scan credit balance
  • Export credit balance
  • India one-time payment
  • Admin-created Stripe arrangement
  • Manual MapThru support or finance decision reflected in Stripe

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • The app can determine account subscription access.
  • The app can determine whether a project has published hosting.
  • The app can show scan credit balance.
  • The app can show export credit balance.
  • India one-time payment access is clear.
  • Non-active billing states are handled clearly.
  • Support can understand why access is allowed or blocked.

issues.main_description_html:

Example Billing Catalog API

Description: Returns a list of active Stripe prices and their associated products. This is a public endpoint used to display available billing options on the website before checkout.

Example cURL Request

curl -X GET http://localhost:9999/v1/billing/catalog \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 123,
  "data": {
    "catalog": [
      {
        "id": "price_1...",
        "unit_amount": 9900,
        "currency": "usd",
        "recurring": {
          "interval": "month"
        },
        "product": {
          "id": "prod_...",
          "name": "Pro Plan",
          "description": "Professional features",
          "metadata": {}
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

Error Responses

Internal Error:

{
  "statusCode": 500,
  "requestTime": 45,
  "data": {
    "error": "failed to fetch catalog"
  }
}

Implementation: Stripe Billing Catalog API

Overview

This task provides the MapThru frontend with the available billing options (such as subscription plans, credits, or hosting packages) before the user initiates a checkout process.

Code Implementation

Rather than duplicating Stripe's catalog system into local relational databases (which requires complex webhook synchronization and invites data staleness), the Catalog API retrieves data directly from Stripe.

  1. Endpoint Logic (src/action/v1/billing/catalog.go):

    • A public GET /catalog route was created since users should be able to view pricing without logging in.
    • It utilizes the stripe-go/v78/price package to list available prices.
    • The query parameters specifically enforce Active: stripe.Bool(true), ensuring that legacy or retired pricing tiers are never displayed to new users.
    • The product details are eagerly loaded by expanding the product reference: params.AddExpand("data.product").

  2. Data Transformation:

    • The Stripe API response is iterated, parsed, and mapped into a simplified JSON structure that the frontend can easily consume (returning the id, unit_amount, currency, recurring interval, and nested product metadata).

Reliability

By querying Stripe directly as the source of truth, the system guarantees 100% accuracy in pricing and item availability, seamlessly handling differences like regional (Canada/India) pricing configured directly in the Stripe Dashboard.

﻿## Document Paths

  • Brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_catalog_api_brainstorming.md
  • Implementation plan: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_catalog_api_plan.md
  • Branch: product-docs
  • Master billing brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md

Purpose

Create an API that lets the MapThru website show the available billing options before a user starts a purchase.

The catalog should be simple and focused. It should expose the plans and paid items that are allowed in the first version: account subscription plans, published project hosting, scan credits, and export credits.

Expected Experience

When the website requests the billing catalog, the API should return the billing options that apply to the current user or account.

The response should make it clear which items are:

  • Account subscription plans
  • Published project hosting
  • Scan credit packages
  • Export credit packages
  • Available for recurring subscription
  • Available for one-time payment
  • Available for Canada tax-aware checkout
  • Available for India one-time payment

The website uses this information to build the custom billing page. The user should not need to log in to Stripe to choose a plan or paid item.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • The website can show available subscription plans.
  • The website can show published project hosting.
  • The website can show scan credit packages.
  • The website can show export credit packages.
  • Canada and India catalog differences are clear.
  • The user can choose billing items in MapThru before Stripe processes payment.
  • The catalog does not expose unsupported first-version add-ons.

issues.display_title: Issue #45: Implement Stripe Billing Checkout API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/07/26

✅ Implementation:

Example Billing Checkout API

Endpoint: POST /v1/billing/checkout
Description: Starts a Stripe checkout session for the authenticated user to subscribe to a plan. Silently creates a Stripe customer record if one does not already exist.

Example cURL Request

curl -X POST http://localhost:9999/v1/billing/checkout \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_session_token>"

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "requestTime": 123,
  "data": {
    "url": "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_..."
  }
}

Error Responses

Unauthorized (No session token):

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "requestTime": 15,
  "data": {
    "error": "unauthorized"
  }
}

Internal Error:

{
  "statusCode": 500,
  "requestTime": 45,
  "data": {
    "error": "failed to create checkout session"
  }
}

Implementation: Stripe Billing Checkout API

Overview

This API initiates a secure Stripe checkout session when an authenticated user decides to purchase a plan or credits.

Code Implementation

The logic is cleanly decoupled into its own file to handle session negotiation.

  1. Customer Resolution (src/action/v1/billing/shared.go):

    • The API uses a helper getStripeCustomer(user) to safely determine if the user already has a mapped StripeCustomerID in the database.
    • If not, it provisions a new customer directly on Stripe using customer.New(), linking their internal user_id via Stripe Metadata, and saves the new Stripe ID back to the local User database.

  2. Checkout Session Creation (src/action/v1/billing/checkout.go):

    • A POST /checkout endpoint constructs a stripe.CheckoutSessionParams payload.
    • The Mode is set to subscription (which can be abstracted further if one-time payments are introduced).
    • Dynamic Redirection: It dynamically constructs the SuccessURL and CancelURL using the shared getFrontendURL() helper, ensuring seamless redirection back to the MapThru client across local, staging, and production environments.

Success Criteria Met

  • The user is securely transported to Stripe's hosted checkout to complete the payment.
  • The checkout session correctly maps to the existing user identity to ensure future webhooks update the correct MapThru account.

﻿## Document Paths

  • Brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_checkout_api_brainstorming.md
  • Implementation plan: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_checkout_api_plan.md
  • Branch: product-docs
  • Master billing brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md

Purpose

Create an API that starts the Stripe purchase process after a user confirms a purchase on the MapThru website.

The website owns the plan, hosting, and credit selection experience. Stripe owns secure payment processing.

Expected Experience

The user selects billing items on the MapThru website and confirms the purchase.

After confirmation, the website asks the API to start checkout. The API should prepare the Stripe purchase using the selected plan, hosting, credits, country rules, billing details, and project assignment where needed.

Stripe then processes the payment or subscription. After the purchase result is known, MapThru should update the account or project access.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • Users choose plans, hosting, and credits inside MapThru.
  • Stripe processes confirmed purchases.
  • Recurring account subscriptions can be started.
  • Published project hosting can be purchased for the intended project.
  • Scan credits and export credits can be purchased.
  • Canada purchases support tax/accounting requirements.
  • India purchases complete as one-time payments with no recurring renewal.
  • Unsupported purchase combinations are rejected clearly.

Implementation: Stripe Billing History API (Task #46)

Overview

This API exposes the billing and transaction history for an authenticated user, allowing them to review past invoices, amounts paid, and download PDF receipts without needing administrative intervention.

Code Implementation

Similar to the Catalog API, the History API avoids mirroring complex transactional ledgers locally and instead relies on Stripe's immutable invoice history.

  1. Endpoint Logic (src/action/v1/billing/history.go):

    • The GET /history route is heavily authenticated. It verifies the user session and retrieves their mapped StripeCustomerID.
    • If a user has no Stripe ID, it returns an empty history array rather than failing.
    • It utilizes stripe-go/v78/invoice to list all invoices associated with the customer: params := &stripe.InvoiceListParams{ Customer: stripe.String(user.StripeCustomerID) }.

  2. Graceful Degradation for Inactive Products:

    • By fetching historical invoices directly, the API natively handles inactive products. Even if a product is archived from the catalog, its historical invoice remains perfectly intact on Stripe, preserving the amount, currency, and timestamps for accounting and tax purposes.

Output

The API formats the raw Stripe invoice models into a concise list of fiber.Map objects containing:

  • id
  • amount_paid / amount_due
  • currency
  • status
  • created_at
  • hosted_invoice_url & invoice_pdf (for direct downloading/viewing)

﻿## Document Paths

  • Brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_history_api_brainstorming.md
  • Implementation plan: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_history_api_plan.md
  • Branch: product-docs
  • Master billing brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md

Purpose

This API should focus on invoices, payment records, tax/accounting visibility, purchased hosting, purchased credits, and key billing events.

The history should include:

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • Users can understand recent purchases.
  • Support can review billing status without guessing.

  • India one-time payments are clearly visible as non-recurring.
  • Published project hosting purchases show the related project.
  • Scan credit and export credit purchases are clear.
  • Billing history helps explain access decisions.

issues.display_title: Issue #47: Implement Stripe Billing Webhook API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/07/26

✅ Implementation:

Example Billing Webhook API

Endpoint: POST /v1/billing/webhook
Description: A public endpoint intended exclusively for Stripe to send subscription lifecycle events. Security is enforced by verifying the Stripe-Signature header against the configured webhook secret.

Events Handled

  • customer.subscription.created
  • customer.subscription.updated
  • customer.subscription.deleted

Example cURL Request (Simulation)

curl -X POST http://localhost:9999/v1/billing/webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Stripe-Signature: t=1620000000,v1=..." \
  -d '{
    "type": "customer.subscription.created",
    "data": {
      "object": {
        "id": "sub_1...",
        "customer": "cus_1...",
        "status": "active"
      }
    }
  }'

Success Response

Returns a raw HTTP 200 status with no JSON body if the webhook is successfully verified and processed.

Error Responses

Bad Request (Missing or invalid signature):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "requestTime": 5,
  "data": {
    "error": "invalid signature"
  }
}

Implementation: Stripe Billing Webhook API

Overview

The Webhook API serves as the automated synchronization engine, listening for real-time lifecycle events from Stripe (such as successful payments, renewals, or cancellations) and updating the MapThru database accordingly.

Code Implementation

The implementation is designed for extreme fault tolerance and security.

  1. Cryptographic Validation (src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go):

    • The endpoint intercepts the raw payload body and validates it against the Stripe-Signature header using webhook.ConstructEvent(). This guarantees that the event is genuinely from Stripe and has not been tampered with.

  2. Idempotent Database Operations:

    • When a customer.subscription.created or updated event occurs, the system utilizes a GORM clause.OnConflict (Upsert) mapped to the stripe_subscription_id.
    • This ensures that if Stripe sends duplicate events, or concurrent webhooks fire simultaneously, the database strictly updates the existing record instead of throwing constraint errors or creating duplicate active subscriptions.

  3. Intelligent Timestamp Handling:

    • To support the latest Stripe API versions (e.g., 2025-03-31), the webhook smartly attempts to parse the CurrentPeriodStart. If the data arrives as 0 (due to period properties moving to line items), the system gracefully falls back to the subscription's .Created timestamp.

  4. Infinite Retry Prevention:

    • If the webhook receives an event for a stripe_customer_id that does not exist in the local database, it safely discards the event but returns a successful HTTP 200 acknowledgment. This stops Stripe from aggressively retrying unprocessable payloads and polluting the error logs.

﻿## Document Paths

  • Brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_webhook_api_brainstorming.md
  • Implementation plan: docs/API/billing/stripe_billing_webhook_api_plan.md
  • Branch: product-docs
  • Master billing brainstorming: docs/API/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md

Purpose

Create an API that receives Stripe billing events and keeps MapThru billing access in sync.

Stripe is the billing source of truth, so MapThru should listen for Stripe changes instead of relying only on the user's checkout screen.

Expected Experience

When Stripe sends a billing event, the API should process it and update the billing state MapThru uses for access checks and history.

The API should handle events related to:

  • Successful payments
  • Failed payments
  • Pending payments
  • Recurring subscriptions
  • Subscription cancellation
  • Past due subscriptions
  • One-time India payments
  • Published project hosting purchases
  • Scan credit purchases
  • Export credit purchases
  • Canada tax and invoice records
  • Admin-created Stripe changes

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • Stripe events keep MapThru billing status current.
  • Duplicate events do not create duplicate access or duplicate credits.
  • Successful purchases grant the expected access.
  • Failed, canceled, expired, or past due billing states are reflected clearly.
  • India one-time payment access is handled separately from recurring subscriptions.
  • Canada invoice and tax records remain visible for accounting review.
  • Support can understand what happened from billing event history.
